contracts_used: Named in the targets only, all from brief H-7: SourceFullCorrect (ChainLiftStatement, RecordLiftStatement), FrameReadBack and DecoderAgreement (OriginStatement). IND$, INT-CTXT, HMAC-PRF and Extract-on-uniform32 appear only as advantages of explicit reductions; the BLAKE2b ROM is the lazily sampled shared cache of the world. The 21 theorems use no contract. No assumption or contract is added.
deviations_from_plan: CtxPrivLiftStatement is stated for both observation modes against randomRecords (equal to idealRecords in mode P by idealRecords_P), not only for mode P against idealRecords, so that the mode-O IND$ step of decision D2 has a named statement.

OriginStatement is a one-world event bound (zero for the produced form, guessTerm and publicationTerm for the published form) and HidingStatement an exact law equality with derived Boolean and event forms (hiding_advantage, hiding_event); neither is a two-sided comparison of two worlds, which is not their natural form.

The targets take their reductions and bill functions as parameters; closed-form bills and the concrete simulator-built reductions are fixed by the delivering stages. A target with artificial reductions is satisfiable trivially and is not a deliverable (guide, design panel section 1).
The view adds the environment state and the handle-to-slot map to the CE-12 analysis projection (needed by R6 and the origin event); this strengthens the targets.
R6 forms are not part of S1 (stage S6).
The bills include the decision coin cost (BillInput.decision), since reductions run the decision.
not_proved: Every target: chain_lift, ctx_lift (both halves), record_lift, idealRecords_origin, idealRecords_hiding.
